items.headline: ASHAs reject CM's appeal, sit-in continues
items.text: On day 11, ASHA workers said they will not leave Freedom Park until an official pay order is issued. The CM urged them to return to work: 'We will keep our word.'

photo.alt: A large domed granite government building with columns and an Indian flag, behind a fenced lawn under a cloudy sky.
photo.caption: Vidhana Soudha, seat of Karnataka's government in Bengaluru, in 2019. File photo.

items.place: Geku and Komkar, Upper Siang, Arunachal Pradesh
items.headline: Siang villages boycott dam consultation meetings
items.text: Geku and Komkar villagers declined officials' dam meetings; students marched in six districts on 27 Nov for arrested students' release. Officials say the meetings covered a survey and a development package.

photo.alt: A wide, calm river between forested hills, with tall grass in the foreground.
photo.caption: The Siang river in Arunachal Pradesh, in 2019. File photo.

items.headline: Mother of man killed by police begins fast
items.text: Asha Devi, whose son was killed in a June police 'encounter', began a fast-unto-death on 27 Nov, saying promised action never came. Police say they fired in self-defence; a judicial inquiry was ordered.

items.headline: Court rebukes police over prisoner's missed cancer care
items.text: A prisoner with cancer missed his AIIMS follow-up as police sent no escort despite 34 jail requests, the High Court found. Two police officers were suspended; the DGP ordered an inquiry.

items.headline: Forum urges deleted voters to refuse police checks
items.text: A voting-rights forum urged people cut from Bengal's rolls not to give papers to police. The Election Commission says the checks are not at its behest; in most cases police showed no order.

items.place: Yassin, East Darfur, and West Kordofan, Sudan
items.headline: Rights monitor reports 14 killed in village raids
items.text: The Sudan Human Rights Observatory says RSF attacks over three days killed 14 people: 12 in East Darfur villages and 2 in West Kordofan. The RSF did not comment.

items.place: El Obeid, North Kordofan, and Damazin, Blue Nile, Sudan
items.headline: 383,000 fled Kordofan in a year, IOM says
items.text: IOM says over 383,000 people fled Kordofan in a year, 15,000 this month. Stray bullets hit three people in a Damazin camp. No government response was reported.

photo.alt: A wide road with street lights under a dark blue sky, a coach approaching and a man walking on the verge.
photo.caption: A main road in El Obeid, North Kordofan, in 2020. File photo of the city.

items.place: Jabalia, Rafah and Gaza City, Gaza
items.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least four in Gaza
items.text: Strikes on Jabalia, Rafah and Gaza City killed 4 (Al Jazeera) to 8 (WAFA) Palestinians on 27 Nov, counting bodies recovered in Rafah. No Israeli military statement was reported.

photo.alt: Flattened concrete buildings and heaps of rubble under a blue sky, with damaged tower blocks behind.
photo.caption: Destroyed buildings in Jabaliya camp, northern Gaza, in October 2024. File photo.

items.place: Mwenga territory, South Kivu, DR Congo
items.headline: Rebels block main road, cutting Mwenga supplies
items.text: Mwenga civil society says FRN rebels (formerly AFC/M23) have blocked the RN2 road since 14 Nov, cutting food supplies and market access. No response from the rebels or the army was reported.

items.place: Juan Santamaría airport, Alajuela, Costa Rica
items.headline: UN rapporteur refused entry, held at airport
items.text: Costa Rica refused entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who spent two nights at the airport. Migration officials cite a 'national security risk' without evidence; the UN rights chief urged reversal.

items.place: Hato Rey, San Juan, Puerto Rico
items.headline: Thousands march over power costs in San Juan
items.text: Organisers say over 8,000 marched over power rates and services and blocked a highway for an hour; no official count or arrests were reported. Officials said they respect the right to protest.

items.place: South of El Hierro, Canary Islands, Spain
items.headline: Migrants found dead on boat off El Hierro
items.text: Between 8 and 14 people were found dead on a boat from Gambia south of El Hierro; about 90 survived. Spain's minister Ángel Víctor Torres cited the 'harshness of the Atlantic route'.

photo.alt: A small harbour with a dark pebble beach, black lava rocks, sailing masts and a breakwater under a bright sky.
photo.caption: The fishing harbour at La Restinga, El Hierro, where most boats land, in 2005.

focus.dek: Geku and Komkar villagers boycotted officials' dam meetings; students marched in six districts on 27 Nov.
